title: Refrigeration and the cold chain
summary: Artificial cooling was first shown in Edinburgh in 1756, but the vapour-compression cycle behind modern refrigerators and air conditioning was first demonstrated by Jacob Perkins, an American working in London, under a British patent of 1834. His machine made ice continuously, though he never sold it. Alexander Twining's trials from 1848 and James Harrison's ice-making machine of 1851 followed, and in the 1870s Carl von Linde's systems began the rapid commercial spread of mechanical refrigeration, which came to replace natural ice for preserving food.

uncertainty.note: From Perkins's 1834 patent to the rapid commercialisation of vapour compression in the 1870s (ASME).

where.modern_name: London, United Kingdom (site of Jacob Perkins's prototype construction and patent filing)
where.historical_name: London, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

importance.justification: Made artificial cold cheap, transforming food storage and later the whole food supply (R4 D3 T3 L2).

beats.caption: Jacob Perkins patents the closed-cycle vapor-compression refrigerator in London, constructing the first working prototype with John Hague.
Refrigerated steamships transport frozen meat from Australia and the Americas to Europe, establishing transoceanic cold chains.
